text: `sudo systemctl status webapp` shows `failed`, and confusingly `sudo systemctl restart webapp` fixes it every time you try. That gap -- broken on boot, fine on a manual restart -- is a clue about *timing*, not the unit's own correctness. `sudo journalctl -u webapp -n 20 --no-pager` shows why it failed in the first place: `/var/lib/app/ready missing -- data-init hasn't completed yet`.

That marker file is created by a separate unit: `sudo systemctl cat data-init.service`. Now check webapp's own ordering: `sudo systemctl show webapp -p After -p Requires`. Neither directive mentions data-init.service -- systemd is free to start both units in parallel at boot, and webapp always loses the race because data-init takes a couple of seconds to actually finish its work.
Add both a hard dependency and an ordering constraint: edit `/etc/systemd/system/webapp.service`'s `[Unit]` section to add `Requires=data-init.service` and `After=data-init.service`.

Reload and verify: `sudo systemctl daemon-reload`, then `sudo systemctl show webapp -p After -p Requires` should list `data-init.service` in both. Note that a `sudo systemctl restart webapp` alone doesn't prove anything at this point -- data-init is already long finished -- the platform's check simulates a genuine fresh race to confirm the ordering actually holds.
